_notes: GAPS WE HAVE DECIDED TO CARRY, AND WHY.
`tools/kb_check.py` fails on propagation defects. Some defects are real
and are not going to be fixed today -- art that costs money to generate,
content waiting on an owner decision. A check that is permanently red is a
check everybody learns to scroll past, which is worse than not having it.
So a gap can be accepted HERE, and only here. An accepted gap is still
PRINTED on every run (as 'gap', not 'ok') -- it is visible, it just does
not fail the build. Accepting one is a deliberate edit to a tracked file,
with a reason and a place where the real work is written down.
Delete an entry the moment the gap closes. kb_check reports an accepted
gap that no longer exists as a FAILURE, so this file cannot rot into a
list of things that were fixed years ago. That guard has already fired
once, on 2026-08-07, when the six missing Case Board images were drawn --
which is the only reason this file is empty rather than stale.
THERE ARE NO ACCEPTED GAPS RIGHT NOW. Keep it that way where you can.
To accept one, add a key with `_why` (several sentences -- why it is not
being fixed, not merely what is missing), `tracked_in` (the doc holding
the real work), and whatever the matching check reads. Only the
`missing_art` key has a reader today; adding a new kind of gap means
teaching the relevant check to look for it.
The wave-2 acceptance (six Chapter 1 back-half ids, accepted 2026-08-08)
was deleted 2026-08-09 when the batch was generated, read and wired --
the guard that fails on healed gaps is why this file is empty again.
